questions.question: Arin alone can do a piece of work in 6 days and Selvi alone can do the same in 8 days. Arin and Selvi undertook to do it for Rs. 7,200. With the help of Kevin, they completed the work in 3 days. How much is to be paid to Kevin?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Arin alone can do a piece of work in 6 days.

Selvi alone can do the same in 8 days.

Arin and Selvi undertook to do it for Rs. 7,200.

With the help of Kevin, they completed the work in 3 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work done by Arin in 1 day = 1/6

Work done by Selvi in 1 day = 1/8

Work done by Arin and Selvi together in 1 day = (1/6) + (1/8) = 7/24

Work done by Arin and Selvi together in 3 days = (7/24) × 3 = 7/8

Work done by Kevin in 3 days = 1 - 7/8 = 1/8

Amount to be paid to Kevin = (1/8) × 7,200 = Rs. 900

**∴ The amount to be paid to Kevin is Rs. 900.**

questions.question: A earns ₹88 per hour and works for 10 hours. B earns ₹95 per hour and works for 8 hours. The ratio of per day wages of A to B is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A earns ₹88 per hour and works for 10 hours.

B earns ₹95 per hour and works for 8 hours.

**Formula Used:**

The ratio of per day wages of A to B = (Per day earnings of A) : (Per day earnings of B).

**Calculation:**

Per day earnings of A = ₹88 × 10

⇒ Per day earnings of A = ₹880

Per day earnings of B = ₹95 × 8

⇒ Per day earnings of B = ₹760

The ratio of per day wages of A to B = ₹880 : ₹760

⇒ The ratio of per day wages of A to B = 880 / 760

⇒ The ratio of per day wages of A to B = 22 : 19

**Therefore, the ratio of per day wages of A to B is 22 : 19.**

questions.question: Tripti can construct a divider alone in 4 days while Rajan can construct it alone in 3 days. If they construct it together and get a payment of Rs. 14000, then what is Tripti's share?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Tripti can construct a divider alone in 4 days, Rajan in 3 days. Total payment = Rs. 14,000.

**Concept:**

The share of each person is proportional to the amount of work they do.

**Calculation:**

Tripti's work rate = 1/4 per day

Rajan's work rate = 1/3 per day

Total work rate = 1/4 + 1/3 ⇒ 7/12 per day

Therefore, Tripti's share = Rs. 14,000 × (1/4 ÷ 7/12) ⇒ Rs. 6,000

**Hence, Tripti's share is Rs. 6,000.**

Priya's share ⇒ (1/12)/(1/4) × Rs. 6000 ⇒ Rs. 2000

**Therefore, Priya's share is Rs. 2000**

questions.question: P, Q and R together can complete a work in 10 days. P alone can complete the work in 30 days. In how many days Q and R together can complete the same work?
questions.solution:
Given,

(P + Q + R) can complete a work in 10 days.

⇒ (P + Q + R)’s one day work = 1/10

P alone can complete the work in 30 days.

⇒ P’s one day work = 1/30

⇒ (Q + R)’s one day work = (1/10 - 1/30) = (3 - 1)/30 = 2/30 = 1/15

Q + R can complete the same work in 15 days.

questions.question: A, B, and C, working alone can do a piece of work in 15, 30 and 75 days respectively. They work together and get Rs. 1615 for completing the work. What is the difference in shares of A and C?
questions.solution:

A, B, and C, working alone can do a piece of work in 15, 30 and 75 days respectively.

They work together and get Rs. 1615 for completing the work.

**Formula used:**

Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

Time ratio of A, B and C = 15 : 30 : 75

As we know,

Efficiency ratio is inversely proportion to time.

Efficiency ratio of A, B and C = 1/15 : 1/30 : 1/75 or 150/15 : 150/30 : 150/75 or 10 : 5 : 2

Efficiency ratio of A, B and C = 10x : 5x : 2x

According to the question

10x + 5x + 2x = 1615

⇒ 17x = 1615

⇒ x = 1615/17

⇒ x = 95

The difference between share A and C = 10x – 2x

⇒ 8x

⇒ 8 × 95

⇒ 760

**∴ The difference in shares of A and C is 760.**

questions.question: A group of men decided to complete a job in 4 days. However, since 10 men dropped out every day, the job got completed at the end of the 7th day. How many men were there in the beginning?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Days to complete job initially = 4

Actual days taken = 7

Men dropping out each day = 10

**Formula used:**

Total Work = Initial Number of Men × Days × Daily Work Rate

Let Initial Number of Men = x

Total Work = x × 4

**Calculations:**

On Day 1: Men = x, Work done = x

On Day 2: Men = x - 10, Work done = x - 10

On Day 3: Men = x - 20, Work done = x - 20

On Day 4: Men = x - 30, Work done = x - 30

On Day 5: Men = x - 40, Work done = x - 40

On Day 6: Men = x - 50, Work done = x - 50

On Day 7: Men = x - 60, Work done = x - 60

Total Work done = x + (x - 10) + (x - 20) + (x - 30) + (x - 40) + (x - 50) + (x - 60)

⇒ Total Work = 7x - (10 + 20 + 30 + 40 + 50 + 60)

⇒ Total Work = 7x - 210

**Setting the total work equal:**

x × 4 = 7x - 210

⇒ 4x = 7x - 210

⇒ 3x = 210

⇒ x = 70

**∴ Initial Number of Men = 70**

Directly Proportional Quantities

When two quantities A and B are directly proportional, their ratio remains constant. A ∝ B ⇒ A / B = k (constant). If one quantity increases, the other increases in the exact same ratio.

Unitary Method

A simple mathematical technique to solve proportional problems by first evaluating the value of a single unit, and then multiplying that value by the required number of units.

Inversely Proportional Quantities

When two quantities A and B are inversely proportional, their product remains constant. A ∝ 1 / B ⇒ A × B = k. For example, time taken to cover a fixed distance is inversely proportional to speed.

questions.question: A and B undertake to do a piece of work for Rs. 330. A can do it in 11 days and B can do it in 22 days. With the help of C, they finish it in 6 days. How much should C be paid for his work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(11, 22, 6) = 66 units.

Efficiency: A = 66 ÷ 11 = 6, B = 66 ÷ 22 = 3, (A+B+C) = 66 ÷ 6 = 11.

Efficiency of C = 11 − (6 + 3) = 2 units.

Wage ratio A : B : C = 6 : 3 : 2 (Total 11 parts = Rs. 330).

C's share = 2 parts = (330 ÷ 11) × 2 = Rs. 60.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 11 days

Time taken by B = 22 days

Time taken by A, B, and C together = 6 days

Total contract value = Rs. 330

**Formula Used:**

Wages are distributed in the ratio of the work done. If the number of days worked is the same for all, wages are divided in the ratio of their one-day work (efficiencies).

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 11
 66
 66 ÷ 11 = 6
 
 

 B
 22
 66 ÷ 22 = 3
 
 

 A + B + C
 6
 66 ÷ 6 = 11
 
 

⇒ Efficiency of C = Efficiency of (A + B + C) − Efficiency of A − Efficiency of B

⇒ Efficiency of C = 11 − 6 − 3 = 2 units/day

⇒ Ratio of efficiencies of A : B : C = 6 : 3 : 2

⇒ Total efficiency parts = 6 + 3 + 2 = 11 parts

⇒ Total wages for 11 parts = Rs. 330

⇒ Value of 1 part = 330 ÷ 11 = Rs. 30

⇒ C's share (2 parts) = 2 × 30 = Rs. 60

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in proportion to the total work done by an individual. If all individuals work together for the same duration, their wages are distributed precisely in the ratio of their efficiencies.

LCM Method in Time and Work

Assuming the Total Work to be the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the given times is a powerful technique because it eliminates fractional calculations, making individual efficiency an easy integer value.

Efficiency vs Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a job. A person who takes fewer days to complete a piece of work has a higher efficiency and consequently earns a larger share of the total wages.

questions.question: A can complete 3/4th of the work in 9 days and B can complete 2/5th of the work in 12 days. With the help of C, all three together complete the whole work in 60/11 days and earn Rs. 330. If money is shared in the ratio of work done, then find the difference in the share of C and the share of A (approximately).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A's time = 9 days for 3/4th work,

B's time = 12 days for 2/5th work,

A + B + C's time = 60/11 days,

Total earnings = Rs. 330

**Concept:**

Shares of A, B, C are proportional to the amount of work they did in the given time

**Calculation:**

Calculate the total shares of A, B, and C.

Time taken by A to complete the whole work = 9 × 4/3 = 12 days

Time taken by B to complete the whole work = 12 × 5/2 = 30 days

Time taken by all three = 60/11 days

LCM of 12, 30, and 60/11 = 60

So, Let the total work be 60 units

Efficiency of A = 60/12 = 5

Efficiency of B = 60/30 = 2

Efficiency of all three = 60/(60/11) = 11

Efficiency of C = Eff.(A+B+C) - Eff.(A + B)

⇒ Efficiency of C = 11 - (5+2)

⇒ 11 - 7 = 4

Thus, Efficiency of C = 4 units

Now, the amount of work done by A in 60/11 days ⇒ 5 × 60/11 = 300/11

The amount of work done by B in 60/11 days ⇒ 2 × 60/11 = 120/11

The amount of work done by C in 60/11 days ⇒ 4 × 60/11 = 240/11

Ratio of work done of A, B, and C =300/11 : 120/11 : 240/11 = 5 : 2 : 4

Since, Total shares = Sum of the ratio of work done,

So, Sum of ratio of work done = 5 + 2 + 4 = 11 units

⇒ Total shares = 11 units

⇒ 330 = 11 units

⇒ 1 unit = 30

⇒ A's share = 30 × 5 = Rs. 150

⇒ C's share = 30 × 4 = Rs. 120

The difference in the share of A and C = 150 - 120 

⇒ Rs. 30

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 30**

**∴ Anjali's share is Rs. 1100.**
